properties.name: When the owner's choice rests on things reflow2 can check (a passing check, a limit, a computation record, a proof), it is recorded as a stated step concluding the Decision; a plain preference stays a sentence
properties.statement:
Anthony, 2026-10-16, keeping option (c) of dec:idea-the-owners-choice-of-a-recommendation-is-recorded-as-a-line-of-reasoning ("Keep both, build after A2").

WHAT MUST BE TRUE:
1. When a choice rests on premises reflow2 computes a truth for, the settling step records a stated step. Such premises are a passing check, a constraint, an accepted decision, an accepted requirement read as its owner's intent, a kept computation record or a confirmed proof. (Revised 2026-10-24 by dec:a-premise-says-whether-it-rests-on-intent-or-delivery; until then this item said "a met requirement". A premise of a step that concludes a Decision reads as the owner's INTENT unless it is marked `delivery`: a requirement, capability or interface then holds on its owner's acceptance, not on being built.) The step's premises are those records, its warrant is the owner's words, and its conclusion is the Decision.
2. A choice that rests on a preference stays the `chose` text. A step over premises reflow2 cannot evaluate would read the decision as unsupported.
3. Once recorded, a premise that stops holding makes the decision's support visibly broken (conclusion_does_not_follow), so a choice whose basis disappeared is noticed.

The acceptance itself stays the owner's word: status and approver, unchanged. Built after A2 (the line-of-reasoning skill and its demonstration).
